item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: Operator request (verbatim intent): inventory-client's listItems(transport) must still resolve to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null (or absent), passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. The inventory-api member of this initiative adds the server side; follow the shared contract exactly. Add tests with a fake transport covering multiple pages, a single page, and an absent next_cursor. Update the README to document the change. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit the change in this repository.

pr._note: pr.title and summary do not mention any tool; the body names no model or tool
pr.body: Approach: client.js listItems loops over GET /items. The first request sends no query; each next request sends {cursor} with the previous next_cursor unchanged. It stops when next_cursor is null or absent. It rejects when a page has no items array, next_cursor is a non-string, a cursor repeats (tracked in a Set, so non-adjacent cycles are caught), or a page returns non-200 (via request). Files: client.js, test/client.test.js (fake paginated transport: multi-page order and cursor sequence, single page with null and with absent next_cursor, repeated cursor, A->B->A cycle, later page failure), README.md (documents the pagination). Checks: npm test 9/9 on e6d5abc. Assumptions: the server follows the shared contract; listItems does not send limit. Open: the cycle test has no timeout, so a regression would hang rather than fail (non-blocking follow-up). inventory-api is a separate repo and not part of this change.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across pages. before: first page only. now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, passing it back unchanged, and rejects repeated cursors.
pr.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination

risk.why: Only client.js listItems changes behaviour; it now makes several requests per call and can reject on malformed pages. The public signature and return type are unchanged. The first review failed on the cycle gap, which was fixed and re-reviewed (pass). Tests cover the new behaviour, and the level stays medium rather than low because callers now see multiple requests and new rejections. Reviewer agt_01M7W9BV8R190QJQSJC519S7MM rated the fix delta low; the whole change is medium.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Operator request (verbatim intent): GET /items in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination. Accept optional query params `limit` (integer 1..100, default 20) and `cursor` (opaque string from a previous response). Body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items stay ordered by `id`; next_cursor is null on the last page. An invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add tests covering paging, last page, limit bounds, and invalid inputs. Update the README to document the change. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit the change in this repository. Follow the shared contract exactly.

pr.body: Approach: api.list_items parses limit and cursor via _parse_limit and _parse_cursor, which raise ValueError turned into a 400 error body. Cursor is the id of the last item on the previous page; the next page is items with id greater than it. next_cursor is set only when more items remain. Key files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 10 tests OK on the committed head. Assumptions: the cursor is a plain decimal id, which clients treat as opaque. Review (agt_01M7W9B3HRAFC5TZ9PDQRDA3R1): pass, no blocking findings. Follow-ups: oversized digit strings return Python int-conversion text in the 400 body; leading-zero cursors are accepted; non-string query values return 400.
pr.summary: GET /items now pages results. before: all items in one response. now: limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor, with next_cursor null on the last page; invalid limit or cursor gives 400.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: Changes the public GET /items response shape (adds next_cursor) and the default page size from all items to 20, so existing callers that expect every item will see different results. Touches api.py, test_api.py and README.md. Behaviour changes, with 10 tests passing. Reviewer confirmed high and did not change the level.
